Building and publishing packages¶

The project builds a pure-Python wheel and source distribution. A GitHub Actions job builds both, checks their metadata/README with Twine, and installs the wheel in an isolated environment for a bounded solver run. CI validates artifacts; the separate manual publishing workflow uploads a release only when dispatched. The repository version is currently 1.0.0; confirm that version and project-name ownership before the first public release.

From a clean checkout:

uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra docs --extra release
uv run --locked black --check .
uv run --locked python -m pytest -q -W error::RuntimeWarning --cov --cov-report=xml
uv run --locked python -m sphinx -b html -W --keep-going docs build/manual
uv build --no-sources
uv run --locked --extra release python -m twine check --strict dist/*

Use an empty dist/ directory for each release so old artifacts cannot be uploaded accidentally. Install both distributions in fresh environments outside the checkout, check imports and poly-mpm modern_ball, and inspect the rendered package description. A full example produces output; use a temporary directory. CI checks the wheel; the publishing workflow checks both the wheel and sdist.

Trusted Publishing workflow¶

.github/workflows/pypi.yml builds, checks, and publishes using PyPI Trusted Publishing. The configured pending publisher uses benjym/poly-mpm, workflow pypi.yml, and no GitHub environment. The publishing job deliberately has no environment field so its OIDC identity matches that configuration. Only that job receives id-token: write; it downloads the tested distributions without checking out or executing project source. No API token is required.

To publish an approved version:

  1. Set the intended version in pyproject.toml, update uv.lock, and push the tested release source to main. Inspect the package description and contents; check documentation links as rendered on PyPI.

  2. Open Actions → Publish to PyPI → Run workflow, select main, and enter the exact version from pyproject.toml.

  3. The workflow checks formatting/tests, builds wheel and sdist, checks metadata, and installs/runs each distribution outside the checkout. Publication runs only after those checks pass. A dispatch on another branch is skipped.

  4. Verify installation from PyPI and create release notes for that version.

The workflow runs only by manual dispatch. Pushing commits or creating tags does not publish. PyPI versions cannot be overwritten; increment the version for a new release. Adding this workflow does not itself create or upload a release.

Before the first release, confirm PyPI project ownership and metadata, review the README rendering/links, and consider a TestPyPI rehearsal with a separately configured publisher. The existing pending publisher is for production PyPI. If you add a protected GitHub environment later, update both the publisher and workflow to the same environment name.

See PyPI Trusted Publishing for the OIDC identity requirements. CODECOV_TOKEN is used only by coverage CI and provides no package-publishing access.
